newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to sell Emetel privatization terms in June.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to sell Emetel privatization terms in June.

text.p: Ecuador said Tuesday the terms for the sale of a 35 percent stake in its telephone company Emetel would go on sale June 3.

"In the beginning the sale of terms was set for May 19, but it was postponed for two weeks to give the National Telecommunications Council time to note observations by bidders and make any changes," National Modernatization Council head Raul Gangotena told reporters.
"We haven't postponed the date of the sale of 35 percent of Emetel shares, which continues to be September this year," he added.
Gangotena said the terms will cost $30,000 and the reference price for the company would be announced shortly after the terms go on sale.

The privatization was originally scheduled for April but was suspended when Congress dismissed former President Abdala Bucaram in February after mass protests against austerity reforms and corruption scandals.
U.S. companies MCI and GTE, Italy's Stet, Telefonica de Espana and Korea Telecom all signed up for the Emetel partial privatization last November.

Gangotena said a recent tour of U.S. cities to visit interested bidders had shown strong interest in the privatization. "This sharp competition is the best guarantee the sale of the shares is good for the country," he said.
Emetel will be split in two operational units and the state will keep a 55 percent share, offering 10 percent to company employees.
Only seven out of 100 residents have a telephone in Ecuador, giving it one of the lowest lines-per-capita ratios in Latin America.
